dialogues.speaker: "Basement Dweller" and "Pauper"
dialogues.text: (I wonder why there are a hedgehog and a cat on the train. Are they a passenger's pets...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe I should stay away.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Excuse me, you two...

dialogues.speaker: "Basement Dweller" and "Pauper"
dialogues.text: (The hedgehog and the cat don't even look at you.)

dialogues.speaker: "Basement Dweller" and "Pauper"
dialogues.text: (The most terrible suffering lies precisely here — in the clear knowledge that there is no hope of an answer, no hope of love. Indifference is the pain of no longer being able to love.)

dialogues.speaker: "Basement Dweller" and "Pauper"
dialogues.text: (They are so arrogant... so cold and detached, as if they simply cannot understand you.)

dialogues.speaker: "Basement Dweller" and "Pauper"
dialogues.text: (Though, in truth, they can't. The hedgehog and the cat don't know what you're saying. They are just a hedgehog and a cat.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Leave quietly.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dear hedgehog, could you please tell me...

dialogues.speaker: Basement Dweller
dialogues.text: (The hedgehog remains motionless, curled up on the soft cushion.)

dialogues.speaker: Basement Dweller
dialogues.text: (It might be a sick hedgehog. A malicious hedgehog. An unremarkable hedgehog. Bitterly and futilely occupying a seat that does not belong to it.)

dialogues.speaker: Basement Dweller
dialogues.text: (This is not its seat, nor will it ever be. The cushion is dying, and the hedgehog knows it. That is why it despises itself — almost to the point of hatred.)

dialogues.speaker: Basement Dweller
dialogues.text: (Too much awareness is also a kind of illness. A true, complete illness.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Leave like a hedgehog — coldly, without looking back.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you? What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Pauper
dialogues.text: (The cat lets out a soft meow, but also ignores you.)

dialogues.speaker: Pauper
dialogues.text: (It does not have a seat of its own. Poor cats are always like this, prone to overthinking. They observe the world with different eyes, watching passersby.)

dialogues.speaker: Pauper
dialogues.text: (The poor have no right to refuse true suffering — pain — yet still long for a dignity that was never meant to be theirs.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Leave hopelessly like a cat.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please forgive me. I meant no harm to your dignity.

dialogues.speaker: Pauper
dialogues.text: (The cat does not answer. Perhaps out of anger, wounded pride, or a sense of insult. Not a lack of morality, but a very human reaction.)

dialogues.speaker: Pauper
dialogues.text: (Or perhaps simply because it is only a cat.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Leave hopelessly like a cat.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What nonsense am I saying...
